headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.26 (95% CI: 0.08–0.92), suggesting that selenium is associated with a lower risk of kidney and renal pelvis cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 95.27%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
